messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The bug occurs in the method OpenMapRealVector.ebeMultiply(RealVector) as evidenced by the failing test that uses this method on OpenMapRealVector instances. The implementation of ebeMultiply creates a copy of the vector via the copy constructor OpenMapRealVector(OpenMapRealVector), then iterates over the entries of the copy's internal map using an iterator obtained from OpenIntToDoubleHashMap.iterator().

The iterator's advance() method includes a check for concurrent modification by comparing a stored modification count (referenceCount) to the current modification count of the map (count). If a mismatch is detected, a MathRuntimeException is thrown indicating the map was modified during iteration.

In ebeMultiply, during iteration on line 373, res.setEntry is called which modifies the internal map entries by calling OpenMapRealVector.setEntry. The setEntry method updates the map by either putting or removing an entry, thus changing the map's state and its modification count. Since this modification occurs during iteration using the iterator from the same map, the modification count check in advance() fails, causing a ConcurrentModificationException.

The root cause is the mutation of the map (via setEntry) during iteration using an iterator that is not fail-safe against modifications from the same map instance. The iterator detects the structural change and throws. This is a classic concurrent modification problem due to modifying a collection while iterating over it without proper handling.

Hence, the MathRuntimeException in the test is caused by modifying the entries map inside ebeMultiply while iterating over its iterator, triggering the concurrent modification check in OpenIntToDoubleHashMap.Iterator.advance().

Recent bug reports do not seem related to this issue, so the diagnosis focuses on this direct evidence.

Next, we can suggest which methods need to be fixed.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
